references.text: God promises Abram to give the land to his descendants, the first explicit land promise after Abram came to Canaan.
God makes a covenant with Abram and defines the boundaries of the land He promises to Abram's descendants.
God confirms His covenant with Abraham by promising the entire land of Canaan to his descendants as an eternal possession.
God renews the land promise to Isaac and confirms the oath He swore to Abraham.
God renews the land promise to Jacob and promises him and his descendants the land he is lying on.
God shows Moses the promised land and reminds Him of the promise given to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to give it to their descendants.
By faith, Abraham obeyed the call to go out to the place he would receive as an inheritance, and he lived as a foreigner in the promised land.
The promise to give the land to Abraham is fulfilled as a national instruction to Israel.
The promise of the land to Abraham is fulfilled through Joshua's leadership and strength.
Contrast between wandering to take possession of the land (Abraham) and merely passing through (Moab).
Connection between obedience and entering the land, but with different theological emphasis (condition versus promise).
Ezekiel confirms that the land given to Abraham (Gen 13) is now to be distributed as an inheritance to the tribes.
The promise of the land to Abraham presupposes the messianic promise to give the whole earth as an inheritance.
Moses' mission (Deut 10) is a direct fulfillment of Abraham's mission (Gen 13).
Contrast between God's promise to give the land (Gen 13) and God's judgment over the land (Ezekiel 32).
Connection between obedience and entering the land, but with different theological emphasis (condition versus promise).
Ezekiel's prophecy about the return from exile (Ezekiel 36) is a fulfillment of the promise of the land (Genesis 13).
Judges 18:10 describes a partial fulfillment of the promise of the land given in Genesis 13:17.
Ezekiel's prophecy about the departure (Ezekiel 20) is a fulfillment of the promise of the land (Genesis 13).
Exodus 6:8 confirms that the promise of the land given to Abraham (Genesis 13) is now to be fulfilled.
Leviticus 20:24 confirms that the promise of the land given to Abraham (Genesis 13) is now to be fulfilled.
Deuteronomy 26:15 is a prayer for the blessing of the land promised in Genesis 13:17.
Deuteronomy 1:21 is an exhortation to the people to take possession of the land promised in Genesis 13:17.
Deuteronomy 1:8 is an exhortation to the people to take possession of the land promised in Genesis 13:17.
Ezekiel 48:29 describes the distribution of the land promised in Genesis 13:17.
Luke 1:73 confirms that the promise of the land given to Abraham (Genesis 13) is an oath.
